questions.question: Angle subtended by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 65 degree. What is the angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of this circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The angle subtended by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 65 degrees.

Concept used:

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60540d3e1e27d6485d4a7e19a550368da9fea4f1bc3667d970818556de1b6a08.png] 

Let O, R, and PQ be the centre, a point on the major arc, and the aforementioned chord respectively.

So, the major arc for the PQ chord is PRQ.

Hence, ∠PRQ = 65°

Here, ∠POQ is the angle subtended by the same chord, PQ on the centre of the circle.

According to the concept,

∠POQ = 2 × ∠PRQ

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 65°

⇒ ∠POQ = 130°

∴ The angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of the circle is 130°.

questions.question: Distance of a chord RS from the centre is 20 cm. If the length of this chord is 30 cm, then what will be the diameter of this circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **perpendicular** from the center bisects the **chord**, so half-chord = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

Using **Pythagorean Triplet** (15, 20, 25), the **radius** is 25 cm.

**Diameter** = 2 × **Radius** = 2 × 25 = 50 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Distance** of chord (d) = 20 cm, **Length of chord** (c) = 30 cm.

**Formula Used:** **Radius** (r) = √[d² + (c/2)²]; **Diameter** (D) = 2 × r.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f9011417471d6db380b36ff21b971f0ac0cc92604c0b8509aa20dd9adf9f60b.png] 

⇒ **Half-chord length** (MS) = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ In **right-angled triangle** OMS, OM² + MS² = OS²

⇒ 20² + 15² = **Radius**²

⇒ 400 + 225 = **Radius**²

⇒ **Radius**² = 625

⇒ **Radius** = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ **Diameter** = 2 × 25 = 50 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 50 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chord Perpendicular Property

A **perpendicular** drawn from the center of a circle to a **chord** always bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagoras Theorem

For any **right-angled triangle**, the square of the **hypotenuse** (radius) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides (distance and half-chord).

Circle Diameter

The **diameter** is defined as the longest chord passing through the **center**, and its length is exactly **twice** the radius.</p

questions.question: The angle subtended by a chord on the center of a circle is 180 degrees. What will be the angle subtended by the same chord on the circumference of this circle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Angle subtended by a chord at the centre = 180°

**Concept Used:**

The angle subtended by a chord at the centre is twice the angle subtended on the circumference.

⇒ Angle subtended on the circumference = 180° / 2 = 90°

**Therefore, the angle subtended by the same chord on the circumference is 90°.**

questions.question: In a circle, a ten cm long chord is at a distance of 12 cm from the centre of the circle. The length of the diameter of the circle (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **perpendicular** from the center of a circle to a chord **bisects** the chord.

Half of the chord length = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Using the standard **Pythagorean triplet** (5, 12, 13):

The **radius** of the circle (r) = 13 cm.

**Diameter** of the circle = 2 × r = 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **chord** (AC) = 10 cm

Distance of the chord from the **centre** (OM) = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord: AM = MC = AC ÷ 2

2. **Pythagoras Theorem** in right-angled triangle ΔAMO: OA² = AM² + OM²

3. **Diameter** of a circle = 2 × Radius (r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66354bc09b7f6ca3ed2848d74a664f08dcb8598068ae7be0b7fa14cdc6bc8dd9.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let O be the centre of the circle and AC be the chord of length 10 cm.

OM is the **perpendicular distance** from the centre O to the chord AC, so OM = 12 cm.

⇒ AM = AC ÷ 2

⇒ AM = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm

In the right-angled triangle ΔAMO, by **Pythagoras theorem**:

⇒ OA² = AM² + OM²

⇒ r² = 5² + 12²

⇒ r² = 25 + 144

⇒ r² = 169

⇒ r = √169 = 13 cm

Therefore, the **radius** of the circle is 13 cm.

⇒ Diameter = 2 × r

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 13 = 26 cm

**Incorrect Options Explanation:**

The value **20 cm** is incorrect because it corresponds to a radius of 10 cm, which does not satisfy the Pythagorean relation with a distance of 12 cm.

The value **22 cm** is incorrect because it corresponds to a radius of 11 cm, which does not form a valid right-angled triangle with the given dimensions.

The value **13 cm** is incorrect because it represents the **radius** of the circle, whereas the question asks for the **diameter**.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

A line drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord always bisects the chord. Conversely, the line joining the center to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a² + b² = c². Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Equal Chords and Distance

Chords of a circle that are equal in length are equidistant from the center of the circle. Conversely, chords equidistant from the center are equal in length.</p

questions.question: AC is the diameter of the circle. B is a point on the circumference. If angle BAC is 40°, then what is angle BCA?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AC is the diameter of the circle.

∠BAC = 40°

**Concept used:**

By the properties of a circle, an angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is a right angle. Therefore, ∠ABC = 90°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/628a27e6a020534612667759d0967eeb29679aacb782336d121e157fffb83f3b.png] 

In triangle ABC, the sum of angles in a triangle is 180°. We can use this property to find ∠ABC.

So, ∠BCA = 180° - ∠BAC - ∠ABC

∠BCA = 180° - 40° - 90°

∠BCA = 50°

**Therefore, ∠BCA = 50°.**
